d: Born to a family of farmers, Sayajirao III was handpicked by the British to be the "perfect" puppet king, only to become their greatest internal challenge. He mastered their systems to empower his people, a defiance famously captured at the 1911 Delhi Durbar. While other princes performed elaborate bows in heavy jewels, the King appeared in a plain white tunic, gave a perfunctory nod, and nonchalantly turned his back on the King-Emperor. By staying within the system to fund visionaries like Ambedkar and Aurobindo, he proved that a throne could be a tool for revolution. This is the story of…
